entries.localizedDescription: Create or edit a three-dimensional digital form using vertices or digital sculpting. CAD design to exact dimensions and preparing a finished model for printing are related but separate tasks.

entries.localizedLabel: Shoot analog photographs
entries.localizedDescription: Photograph on film to produce exposed frames for later chemical processing or scanning; the defining feature is the analog photographic process.

entries.localizedLabel: Create animation or stop motion
entries.localizedDescription: Create the illusion of movement by capturing successive frames of a drawing, object, or digital form. Stop-motion involves filming an object in stages; computer animation can be fully digital.

entries.localizedLabel: Take photographs
entries.localizedDescription: Choose a frame and capture still photos with a camera or phone. Developing, retouching, selecting, and publishing are separate stages.

entries.localizedLabel: Edit photographs
entries.localizedDescription: Select and edit existing digital images by cropping, adjusting tone or color, retouching, or compositing. Taking photos and publishing them are separate activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Create graphic design or a poster
entries.localizedDescription: Arrange type, images, and shapes to communicate a visual message or make a poster. Unlike drawing, the result usually serves a communication or layout purpose.

entries.localizedLabel: Create an illustration
entries.localizedDescription: Create an image that explains, accompanies, or visually tells a story about a text or idea. Its purpose is tied to specific material, unlike a free-form sketch.

entries.localizedLabel: Practice calligraphy or lettering
entries.localizedDescription: Create decorative letters and inscriptions with controlled pen, brush, or digital strokes. Lettering usually draws the letterforms; calligraphy builds them through a written stroke technique.

entries.localizedLabel: Make a collage or scrapbook
entries.localizedDescription: Compose an image from cutouts, photographs, paper, or other ready-made elements. Scrapbooking adds captions or keepsakes to an album; a collage can stand alone.

entries.localizedLabel: Create a comic or manga
entries.localizedDescription: Develop and create a sequence of illustrated panels with text for a comic or manga. Story writing, drawing pages, and publishing may be phases of one project.

entries.localizedLabel: Edit or color-grade video
entries.localizedDescription: Select, arrange, and join recorded video and audio clips into a sequence, then adjust color if needed. This is assembling recorded material, not filming it.

entries.localizedLabel: Make a print or screen print
entries.localizedDescription: Prepare a printing plate or stencil and transfer an image from it onto paper or another material. Carving the plate and making print runs are related but distinct phases.

entries.localizedLabel: Develop film or print photographs
entries.localizedDescription: Develop exposed photographic film and/or print a photograph from a negative or digital file onto paper. This is laboratory processing, not taking the photograph.

entries.localizedLabel: Draw or sketch
entries.localizedDescription: Draw by hand with lines or strokes, or make a quick sketch, to depict something observed or imagined. The work does not need to be finished.

entries.localizedLabel: Create digital drawing or digital art
entries.localizedDescription: Create a drawing or painted image with digital brushes or layers on a computer or tablet. Do not treat it as graphic design unless the task is to lay out a message or design.

entries.localizedLabel: Film video
entries.localizedDescription: Capture moving images with a camera, choosing framing, movement, and sound. Editing footage that has already been recorded is a separate operation.

entries.localizedLabel: Paint
entries.localizedDescription: Apply pigment to a surface with a brush, palette knife, or another painting method, developing color, tone, and composition. Digital painting can be tracked separately.

entries.localizedLabel: Do woodworking or carpentry
entries.localizedDescription: Make a wooden object or joint by marking, sawing or planing, drilling, and assembling parts. Furniture joinery differs from turning a rotating workpiece on a lathe.

entries.localizedLabel: Make leather goods
entries.localizedDescription: Cut, punch, sew or fasten, and finish leather to make an item. Shoe repair, making an accessory, and tooling are distinct project types.

entries.localizedLabel: Make props
entries.localizedDescription: Build a prop for a costume, film shoot, or stage production from chosen materials. Wearing or using the prop and staging a scene are separate activities.
localizedAliases: Make a stage or film prop

entries.localizedLabel: Make candles, soap, or paper
entries.localizedDescription: This category covers three crafts: pour or shape a candle with a wick, make soap from a base or ingredients, or produce a sheet of handmade paper. Specify the process when possible; these are not one technique.

entries.localizedLabel: Make a sculpture or sculpted form
entries.localizedDescription: Create a three-dimensional sculptural form by adding or modeling material, carving, assembling parts, or combining methods. Clay and other pliable materials are one approach, not the whole of sculpture.

entries.localizedLabel: Make models or miniatures
entries.localizedDescription: Create a scale model or miniature object to represent a space, scene, or design. Game miniatures may also be used in wargaming, but assembling them is still a craft activity.

entries.localizedLabel: Do metalworking or blacksmithing
entries.localizedDescription: Shape or work metal by cutting, joining, forging, or heating. Blacksmithing, which involves hammering heated stock, is one technique within the broader craft of metalworking.

entries.localizedLabel: Build scale models or dioramas
entries.localizedDescription: Assemble a scale model or diorama from a kit or parts, fitting and painting them to represent an object or scene. Assembly and painting may be separate project stages.

entries.localizedLabel: Make a mosaic
entries.localizedDescription: Arrange small tiles, pieces of glass, or stone into an image or pattern and attach them to a base. Cutting pieces and grouting may be stages of the project.

entries.localizedLabel: Do origami or paper craft
entries.localizedDescription: Fold paper along creases to make a figure (origami), or cut, glue, or assemble paper into an object (paper craft); these methods are not interchangeable.

entries.localizedLabel: Bind books
entries.localizedDescription: Sew or glue sheets into a book block and make or attach a cover. Repairing an existing binding and making a new book are related variations.

entries.localizedLabel: Restore furniture
entries.localizedDescription: Stabilize and restore existing furniture by repairing joints or damage, removing old finishes, and refinishing it. Making new furniture is a separate goal.

entries.localizedLabel: Assemble or paint models and miniatures
entries.localizedDescription: Assemble a model or miniature from ready-made parts, paint it, or do both as part of a project. Assembly and painting are distinct operations; designing or playing with the finished miniature are different activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Work with glass or make stained glass
entries.localizedDescription: Cut, assemble, and join colored glass pieces, or shape glass into a decorative object. Stained-glass assembly with seams differs from glass fusing or glassblowing.

entries.localizedLabel: Turn wood on a lathe
entries.localizedDescription: Secure a wooden blank on a lathe and remove material with a cutting tool while it rotates to form a symmetrical piece. This is not a general term for all woodworking.

entries.localizedLabel: Carve or cut a design
entries.localizedDescription: Remove material with a chisel or knife to carve a pattern or three-dimensional form in wood, linoleum, stone, or another material. Specify the material and result separately.

entries.localizedLabel: Make jewelry or beadwork
entries.localizedDescription: Make jewelry from metal, wire, stones, findings, or beads, or create beadwork and patterns that are not jewelry. Specify the technique, such as stringing, weaving, embroidery, or setting.

entries.localizedLabel: Do pottery or ceramics
entries.localizedDescription: Shape a clay object by hand or on a pottery wheel, then optionally dry, fire, and glaze it. A full ceramic project may span several sessions.

entries.localizedLabel: Make a costume or cosplay outfit
entries.localizedDescription: Design and assemble a costume or character outfit through sewing, pattern work, or crafting. Wearing it, taking photos, and role-play are separate activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Do cross-stitch
entries.localizedDescription: Embroider a design with repeated diagonal cross-shaped stitches on canvas or even-weave fabric. This differs from free-form satin stitch and embroidery on a preprinted design.

entries.localizedLabel: Make lace
entries.localizedDescription: Create openwork fabric by interlacing threads into patterns, for example with bobbins or a needle. This differs from knitting dense loops.

entries.localizedLabel: Do quilting or patchwork
entries.localizedDescription: A quilt project may include patchwork piecing (sewing a top from fabric pieces) and quilting (stitching the top, batting, and backing together). You can combine both stages in one personal entry or track them separately.

entries.localizedLabel: Sew patchwork
entries.localizedDescription: Cut and sew fabric pieces into a new cloth or item. Unlike quilting, patchwork alone does not require stitching together the layers of a quilt.

entries.localizedLabel: Make macramé
entries.localizedDescription: Create a pattern or object by tying knots in cord or thread, rather than sewing with a needle or knitting.

entries.localizedLabel: Do needlepoint or weave a tapestry
entries.localizedDescription: This textile category covers two scopes: (1) needlepoint, filling canvas with stitches to create an image; and (2) making a tapestry, which may be woven on a loom or frame. Keep the embroidered and woven practices distinct; “tapestry” is not limited to embroidery.

entries.localizedLabel: Dye yarn or fabric
entries.localizedDescription: Color yarn or fabric using a chosen dye application and setting method. The result is a change in the material’s color, not weaving or sewing it.

entries.localizedLabel: Spin fibers into yarn
entries.localizedDescription: Draw out and twist fibers into continuous yarn by hand or with a spindle or spinning wheel. Dyeing the yarn and knitting or weaving with it are later or separate activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Sew clothing
entries.localizedDescription: Take measurements, cut fabric, and sew pieces together to make clothing. Altering or repairing an existing garment may be tracked as a separate goal.

entries.localizedLabel: Make a fabric doll or stuffed toy
entries.localizedDescription: Cut and sew or stuff fabric to make a doll or soft toy. Pattern drafting, an embroidered face, clothing, and finishing are project stages or facets.

entries.localizedLabel: Weave fabric
entries.localizedDescription: Interlace lengthwise warp threads with crosswise weft on a loom or frame to form fabric. Spinning produces yarn, not woven cloth.

entries.localizedLabel: Do Tunisian crochet
entries.localizedDescription: Pick up and work a row of loops with a special long hook, usually holding the row’s loops until the pass is complete. This is a distinct crochet technique, not another name for ordinary crochet.

entries.localizedLabel: Make felt or felted items
entries.localizedDescription: Mat wool fibers together through friction and moisture or with a needle to form dense felt. Specify wet felting or needle felting when useful.

entries.localizedLabel: Crochet
entries.localizedDescription: Pull yarn through loops with a hook to form fabric or motifs. The hook-based loops and construction distinguish crochet from knitting with needles.

entries.localizedLabel: Knit with needles
entries.localizedDescription: Work loops on straight or circular needles to make fabric or an item. The technique and row construction differ from crochet.

entries.localizedLabel: Embroider
entries.localizedDescription: Stitch thread through fabric according to a design to create decorative stitches. Specify the material or pattern separately when useful.

entries.localizedLabel: Create or edit a 3D model or CAD design
entries.localizedDescription: Create or change digital 3D geometry through polygon modeling, digital sculpting, or parametric CAD. Precise part design is one important subtype, not the entire scope of 3D modeling. Physically printing the model is a separate stage.

entries.localizedLabel: 3D-print an existing model
entries.localizedDescription: Prepare a printer and make a physical part from an existing digital file. Track creating the 3D model or configuring slicer settings separately if useful.

entries.localizedLabel: Practice amateur radio
entries.localizedDescription: Set up a radio station or antenna and communicate with other amateur radio operators, or experiment with transmitting and receiving. Passive listening to broadcast radio is separate.

entries.localizedLabel: Do CNC, laser, or vinyl cutting
entries.localizedDescription: Prepare a file or configure and run a digital cutting or engraving operation: CNC milling or cutting, laser cutting or engraving, or vinyl cutting on a plotter. The machine, process, and material are distinct attributes.

entries.localizedLabel: Do woodworking as a maker project
entries.localizedDescription: Cut, shape, join, or finish wood for a personal maker project. Do not assume this means home repair or professional carpentry.

entries.localizedLabel: Work on a DIY project
entries.localizedDescription: Independently design, make, modify, or repair an item by hand or with tools. Specify the actual operation if a broad project includes several unlike stages.

entries.localizedLabel: Repair or improve the home
entries.localizedDescription: Repair or improve a home or household infrastructure, for example by painting, fixing a finish, or installing a fixture. The goal is home maintenance even when hobby tools are used.

entries.localizedLabel: Build electronics or solder a circuit
entries.localizedDescription: Design or assemble an electronic circuit by mounting components on a circuit or prototyping board and soldering when needed. Programming a microcontroller may be a separate stage.

entries.localizedLabel: Customize a personal vehicle as a hobby
entries.localizedDescription: Change the appearance or configuration of a personal vehicle, such as its parts, paint, interior, or equipment, as a project. Routine repair to restore function is a neighboring but different goal.

entries.localizedLabel: Work with microcontrollers
entries.localizedDescription: Connect and program a microcontroller to read sensors or control devices. Basic circuit soldering and a full robotics project may be neighboring tasks.

entries.localizedLabel: Prepare a slicer or run a 3D print
entries.localizedDescription: Prepare a digital 3D model for printing by orienting it, slicing it, or setting printer parameters; printing can then be started, monitored, or finished separately. Slicing, printer setup, and printing are related but need not all happen together.

entries.localizedLabel: Code as a personal creative activity
entries.localizedDescription: Write, debug, or modify code for a personal project or interest. Work tasks and courses may have a different context; playing a created game is a separate use.

entries.localizedLabel: Develop a game or mod as its creator
entries.localizedDescription: Design rules, levels, or narrative, or code a game or mod. Playing it, testing a build, and publishing are related phases of the creative project.

entries.localizedLabel: Repair a tool or personal item
entries.localizedDescription: Diagnose a fault and restore an existing tool or item to working order. Changing its appearance without repairing it may count as customization.
localizedAliases: Fix a tool or personal belonging

entries.localizedLabel: Build or program a robot
entries.localizedDescription: Assemble and program a robotic device by combining a mechanical structure, sensors, and control. Coding alone or a circuit board alone is a component, not a complete robotics project.

entries.localizedLabel: Assemble furniture
entries.localizedDescription: Assemble a piece of furniture from ready-made parts and hardware using instructions or your own plan. Making parts from scratch and installing the furniture at home are related stages.

entries.localizedLabel: Build or modify a PC
entries.localizedDescription: Assemble, replace, or configure personal-computer components such as the case, boards, cooling, or software. Everyday computer use is not PC assembly.

entries.localizedLabel: Assemble, finish, or paint a model
entries.localizedDescription: Remove supports and seams, sand, assemble, prime, or paint model parts that have already been made. Printing or casting the model itself is an earlier stage.

entries.localizedLabel: Upcycle or repurpose an item
entries.localizedDescription: Turn a used item or material into a new object or function while retaining or reusing the material. Ordinary repair restores its previous purpose.

entries.localizedLabel: Maintain a bicycle
entries.localizedDescription: Clean, lubricate, adjust, diagnose, or replace a bicycle’s consumable parts. Riding the bicycle is a separate activity.

entries.localizedLabel: Work on a maker project
entries.localizedDescription: Plan and build a chosen interdisciplinary prototype or object by combining electronics, mechanics, code, or fabrication. Choose a specific stage instead of this general category when it is known.

entries.localizedLabel: Work on projects in a home lab
entries.localizedDescription: Run a personal experiment or build a prototype at a home-lab workbench. The setting alone does not specify whether the task is measurement, assembly, or analysis.

entries.localizedLabel: Rehearse as an ensemble
entries.localizedDescription: Rehearse a piece together in an instrumental or vocal ensemble, coordinating parts, cues, and tempo before a performance. A public concert is a different stage.

entries.localizedLabel: Arrange music or write it in notation
entries.localizedDescription: This category covers either adapting music for chosen voices or instruments (arranging, with or without writing notation) or recording a musical part or work in notation. The activities may be combined but need not occur together.

entries.localizedLabel: Produce or record audio
entries.localizedDescription: Create audio as a production process: recording a source, programming or editing, assembling tracks, and preparing the project may be stages. Recording sound is one option; mixing and mastering remain separate specialized activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Make beats
entries.localizedDescription: Create rhythmic or musical loops and arrangements with a sampler, drum machine, or DAW. Unlike a DJ set, this involves building material rather than only mixing released recordings.

entries.localizedLabel: Perform a DJ set
entries.localizedDescription: Mix and sequence recordings into a continuous music set, coordinating tempo and transitions. Creating new beats and simply listening to music are different activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Play or practice an instrument
entries.localizedDescription: Play music or practice technique on an instrument. Learning a piece and playing freely may overlap, but tuning or repairing an instrument is a different activity.

entries.localizedLabel: Jam with other musicians
entries.localizedDescription: Improvise and play music with others in a free-form or loosely structured jam. Rehearsing fixed ensemble material involves parts prepared in advance.

entries.localizedLabel: Improvise music or on stage
entries.localizedDescription: Invent and perform material without a fully fixed script or score in advance. This may be stage or musical improvisation; a prepared piece is rehearsed instead.

entries.localizedLabel: Sing karaoke
entries.localizedDescription: Perform a song with a backing track or on-screen lyrics in a karaoke format. This is participation in a playback performance, not necessarily voice training or songwriting.

entries.localizedLabel: Take part in an amateur musical
entries.localizedDescription: Participate in an amateur music-and-theater production combining acting, songs, and choreography. Rehearsing and performing publicly are project phases.

entries.localizedLabel: Master audio
entries.localizedDescription: Prepare a completed mix for release or a medium by adjusting overall level and ensuring the final version translates consistently. This is not multitrack mixing.

entries.localizedLabel: Wear a cosplay costume or portray a character
entries.localizedDescription: Wear a cosplay costume and portray or act as a character. Role-play, photo shoots, contest appearances, and attending a festival may be separate or overlapping episodes. Making the costume and preparing a photo shoot are separate activities.
localizedAliases: Portray a character at a shoot, contest, or role-play event

entries.localizedLabel: Tune or maintain a musical instrument
entries.localizedDescription: Tune an instrument and perform basic care or maintenance, such as changing strings, servicing its mechanism, or cleaning it. Playing music on it is separate.

entries.localizedLabel: Organize an amateur concert or production
entries.localizedDescription: Organize an amateur concert or stage production by coordinating participants, venue and time, program, and practical preparations. Performing on stage and attending as an audience member are separate roles.

entries.localizedLabel: Sing on your own
entries.localizedDescription: Sing alone, perform a song or vocal exercise, or practice your voice. Karaoke adds accompaniment or on-screen lyrics; recording vocals is an additional production task.

entries.localizedLabel: Rehearse stage cues and scene transitions
entries.localizedDescription: Run a production or scene in sequence, coordinating entrances, cues, lighting and sound, transitions, and participants. This is a technical ensemble run-through, not only actors learning lines.

entries.localizedLabel: Perform for an audience or at a home concert
entries.localizedDescription: Perform a music or stage program for an audience, including at a home concert. Attending as an audience member and organizing the event are separate activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Work in a digital audio workstation
entries.localizedDescription: Create or edit a music or sound project in a digital audio workstation (DAW), for example by recording, programming MIDI, or editing clips and plugins. Specify a narrower stage separately if useful.

entries.localizedLabel: Rehearse or sing in a choir
entries.localizedDescription: Sing with a choir while learning a piece or parts at rehearsal, or perform them. Rehearsal is one phase, while public or informal choir singing remains in scope too. Solo singing and watching a choir are different activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Rehearse a dance
entries.localizedDescription: Repeat a dance combination or choreography, practicing timing, steps, formations, and musical accents. Creating new choreography and social dancing are different activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Compose music or a song
entries.localizedDescription: Create new instrumental or vocal music by developing melody, harmony, rhythm, and/or form. A song with lyrics is one kind of composition; instrumental music does not require words.

entries.localizedLabel: Sort or study a record collection
entries.localizedDescription: Browse, catalog, compare, and explore a music collection or its editions. Listening to a particular recording may happen at the same time, but organizing the collection is its own activity.
localizedAliases: Study a vinyl and record collection

entries.localizedLabel: Design sound for a scene or work
entries.localizedDescription: Create or select sound effects and atmospheres for a scene, game, or work by shaping timbre and dynamics. This is not songwriting.

entries.localizedLabel: Perform spoken word or poetry
entries.localizedDescription: Perform a poetic or spoken text aloud in rhythmic delivery for listeners or in rehearsal. Music or a beat may accompany it, but the performance does not have to become a song.

entries.localizedLabel: Write or perform stand-up comedy
entries.localizedDescription: Write or edit jokes, develop a stand-up set, or rehearse or perform it for an audience. Creating comedic material and performing it are related but distinct phases.

entries.localizedLabel: Mix audio tracks
entries.localizedDescription: Balance and process separate tracks to create a combined mix, using levels, panning, equalization, and dynamics. This is not final preparation of the master file.

entries.localizedLabel: Rehearse a theater or acting role
entries.localizedDescription: Rehearse a stage role by working through lines, blocking, intonation, movement, and interactions with scene partners. A technical rehearsal of the scene may be a separate task.

entries.localizedLabel: Translate fan works or fan translations
entries.localizedDescription: Translate a work created in a fandom or a fan translation of another work, carrying its meaning and style into another language. Posting the translation online is a separate stage.

entries.localizedLabel: Write fan fiction
entries.localizedDescription: Create a fictional text in an existing fictional universe or featuring its characters, adding an original plot or scene. Publishing and reading fan fiction are separate activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Write poetry
entries.localizedDescription: Compose or edit poems by choosing words, rhythm, imagery, or form. Reading published poetry and publishing your own work are related but separate activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Write a story or novel
entries.localizedDescription: Write a work of fiction, such as a short story or novel. Reading, editing, and publishing the text are other stages.

entries.localizedLabel: Write a script or game narrative
entries.localizedDescription: Write a story, dialogue, or narrative for an interactive work. Game-mechanics design and programming are related but separate tasks.

entries.localizedLabel: Create an original podcast, vlog, or stream
entries.localizedDescription: Create original online media such as a podcast, vlog, or stream. Planning, recording or hosting live, editing, and publishing may be tracked separately, though they can belong to one production project.

entries.localizedLabel: Create fan art
entries.localizedDescription: Create visual work inspired by characters, a world, or a work from a fandom. Drawing, painting, digital illustration, collage, and other media are possible; this is not by default a text post.

entries.localizedLabel: Create and publish personal creative photos or videos
entries.localizedDescription: Create and post photos or videos as personal creative work. Editing, filming, and publishing may be separate project phases.
localizedAliases: Create and publish personal creative photos

entries.localizedLabel: Create a webcomic
entries.localizedDescription: Create a sequential comic for web publication by developing episodes or pages, arranging panels, and making images with or without text. Publishing may be part of the project, but a webcomic is not just a regular text post.

entries.localizedLabel: Keep a journal or write an essay
entries.localizedDescription: Write personal journal entries or essays. Private journaling, creative writing, and public publication can be distinct activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Write or maintain a personal blog
entries.localizedDescription: Run a personal blog by choosing topics and creating or posting entries or updates in your own authored feed. It may be text, photo, video, or mixed media; reading someone else’s blog is a different activity.

entries.localizedLabel: Build, sort, catalog, or study a collection
entries.localizedDescription: Work with a personal or themed collection: find or acquire items, sort or arrange them, catalog them, take them apart or maintain them, or study the collection. A session may involve one or several of these practices; merely owning a collection is not an activity.

entries.localizedLabel: Attend or watch a live cultural performance
entries.localizedDescription: Be in the audience to watch or listen to live theater, dance, a concert, or another cultural performance. Playing, singing, dancing on stage, and rehearsing are participant activities.

entries.localizedLabel: Visit an archaeological or religious heritage site
entries.localizedDescription: Visit and view an archaeological site or a religious or cultural heritage site. The focus is the site or monument; a ritual or worship service is not implied.

entries.localizedLabel: Visit a library
entries.localizedDescription: Go to a library to use its collection, space, or services: find, borrow, or return materials, work at a desk, or attend an event. Reading a book there is a separate concurrent practice.

entries.localizedLabel: Take a guided tour of a landmark
entries.localizedDescription: Take part in a guided account and follow a route around a landmark or complex. Viewing the site may happen at the same time, but traveling there independently is a separate stage.

entries.localizedLabel: Visit a historic site or monument
entries.localizedDescription: View a preserved historic site or monument in person, such as an architectural or memorial site. Attending a religious service or taking a guided tour are other layers of a visit.

entries.localizedLabel: Visit an art gallery
entries.localizedDescription: Go to an art gallery to view displayed visual works or a curated exhibition. This is an art-display venue or format and does not necessarily mean a museum collection.

entries.localizedLabel: Attend a book festival or book fair
entries.localizedDescription: Attend a public book festival or fair for author events, readings, discussions, or browsing exhibitor stands. Buying books and reading are separate activities; a book fair is not the same as an entertainment fair.

entries.localizedLabel: Visit a museum
entries.localizedDescription: Visit a museum to view its permanent collection, temporary exhibitions, or other displays. The subject and whether there is a tour are details of the visit, not limits on the kinds of exhibits.

entries.localizedLabel: Visit an exhibition or biennial
entries.localizedDescription: View a temporary exhibition or biennial as a visitor, moving among selected works and sections. The event may be held in a museum, gallery, or another venue.

entries.localizedLabel: Walk an architectural route
entries.localizedDescription: Walk along a chosen urban architecture route, viewing buildings or spaces; a guide is optional. An architectural walk combines walking and viewing, which may receive overlapping tags.
